claim: IronFlockOS (IronFlock GmbH, Apache-2.0) describes itself as 'a Debian-based appliance OS' that runs the IronFlock device-agent and Docker; 'RAUC writes the new system into the inactive one of two slots' and the device falls back if the agent cannot reach IronFlock from the new slot. Targets: amd64-efi and arm64-efi (shim, GRUB, RAUC), rpi-arm64 (Pi 4/400/5/CM4/CM5, firmware tryboot + RAUC), jetson-orin (NVIDIA UEFI + nvbootctrl + RAUC; 'none yet', Jetson uses Ubuntu 24.04). base image = Debian 13 with Docker CE and RAUC; base-rt = Debian's PREEMPT_RT kernel. No Kubernetes. Status in its own words: 'not at 1.0 yet' and 'No target has passed its hardware acceptance yet'. [partly supersedes C-DEC-013: a public Debian + RAUC appliance OS exists, but it is pre-1.0 and not field-proven]

claim: Peer-reviewed workshop paper (Dewit, Paolillo, Goossens; OSPERT 2024 at ECRTS): Raspberry Pi 5 Model B Rev 1.0 on Debian 12, kernel 6.6.21 with and without PREEMPT_RT, cyclictest -vmn -i100 -p99 -t for 1 h while stress-ng runs all 320+ stressors in parallel and iperf3 floods the network: maximum observed latency 124.00 us with PREEMPT_RT (the text says 125 us) vs 36,802 us stock; averages 5.91 us vs 14.69 us. Authors call the load 'unrealistic' and the kernel 'untuned'. One board, one 1-hour run. [original measurement; complements, does not supersede, the forum rows C-REF-DC-technical-001 / C-REF-DC-robotics-006 (6.13-rc, overnight, >1 ms)]
